note: Every hazard is a standard school-lab safety failure with a real cause. Review the wording and the quiz answers before use.

hazards.title: Chemical splash in the eye
hazards.guided: Stop. Put goggles on before you work with any chemical. They are in the locker.
hazards.happened: Liquid splashes up into your unprotected eyes. The work stops.
hazards.treat: You hold your eyes open under the eyewash and flush them. The real time is 15 minutes, then medical help.
hazards.why: Eyes absorb chemicals fast and damage can begin within seconds. Goggles are the only barrier, and flushing with the eyewash is the first response.

options: Put goggles on before touching any chemical
Turn your head away while pouring
Work faster so there is less time to splash

hazards.title: Chemical on your skin and clothes
hazards.guided: Stop. Put an apron on before you work with chemicals. It is in the locker.
hazards.happened: A drop lands on your sleeve and soaks through to your arm.
hazards.treat: You flush your arm under running water for several minutes and take off the wet clothing.
hazards.why: Splashes are normal in a lab. An apron stops them reaching your skin, and running water dilutes whatever does get through.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do when a chemical touches your skin?
options: Rinse it under running water for several minutes
Wipe it off with a paper towel
Wait to see whether it hurts

hazards.title: Burn from hot glass
hazards.guided: Stop. That container is hot. Pick up the tongs from the rack before you move it.
hazards.happened: You grab the hot beaker bare-handed, flinch, and drop it. It shatters.
hazards.treat: You hold the burn under cool running water for several minutes.
hazards.why: Hot glass looks exactly like cold glass. Anything near a hot plate or just heated should be handled with tongs, and a burn needs cool running water right away.

quiz.q: How can you tell glass is too hot to touch?
options: You can't by looking, so use tongs near any heat source
It will glow or look different
Hover a bare hand over it first

hazards.title: Spill on the bench
hazards.guided: Stop. That would overflow the container. Nothing was added.
hazards.happened: The liquid runs over the rim and across the bench. You stop and mop it up.
hazards.why: A container should never be filled past about two thirds. Use a larger container or a smaller volume.

quiz.q: What should you have checked first?
options: The container's capacity against the volume you were adding
